name: Cognizant
overview: Cognizant is an IT services company that hires a large number of freshers in India. Its fresher hiring and training program is called Generation Cognizant (GenC), which starts new hires with role-based training and then project work. Cognizant says there are no service bonds in the GenC program.
variation_note: Cognizant says not every candidate goes through every step and the process varies by role; rounds, timings and platforms reported by candidates change by year, college and skill cluster.

roles.title: GenC (Programmer Analyst Trainee)
roles.description: Entry-level software role for engineering graduates. New hires are trained in their skill cluster (Java, Python or C# with SQL) before joining projects.

eligibility.text: B.E/B.Tech, M.E/M.Tech, MCA or M.Sc IT students of the current batch (2026 batch on this page)
At least 60% in X, XII, UG and PG
Minimum 60% in X, XII, Diploma, UG and PG; 59.9% is not rounded off
No active backlog at the time of the exam
Overall gap in academics not more than 2 years
Gap between studies not more than 1 year (a different PrepInsta page)
Must be flexible to work from any Cognizant office and in different shifts

compensation.text: 4 LPA, designation Programmer Analyst Trainee (as reported)

roles.title: GenC Pro (Programmer Analyst)
roles.description: Higher category given to candidates who do better in the technical assessment and interview. PrepInsta calls a similar track GenC Elevate.

eligibility.text: Same registration and eligibility as GenC; the category is decided after the technical assessment

compensation.text: GenC Elevate: 4 LPA + skill bonus = 5.4 LPA (as reported)

roles.title: GenC Next (Programmer Analyst)
roles.description: Top fresher category for candidates with stronger coding skills. Candidates report harder live coding in the interview.

eligibility.text: Same registration and eligibility as GenC; the category is decided after the technical assessment

stages.name: Application and screening
stages.what: You apply through your college drive or the off-campus portal (Superset). Recruiters review applications and contact shortlisted students through the placement officer or email.

format.text: Step 1 application, Step 2 initial screening, then assessments, interviews and result

At registration you pick a skill cluster: Cluster 1 Java + ANSI SQL + HTML/CSS/JS (default), Cluster 2 Python + ANSI SQL + Cloud Fundamentals, Cluster 3 C# + ANSI SQL + HTML/CSS/JS; final cluster is Cognizant's decision
2026 off-campus timeline reported: registration from Feb 24, 2026, communication test from Mar 7, aptitude from Mar 10, technical from Mar 11, interviews from Mar 27

study: Pick the skill cluster you can code in best
tips: Your name and date of birth must match your 10th marksheet and PAN
Use a personal email you will keep; it cannot be changed later
stages.before_next: Choose your cluster language and start daily SQL and coding practice in it.
stages.label: Official

stages.name: Communication assessment
stages.what: An automated English test: reading, grammar, listening and speaking. Some tasks play audio once and you repeat it.

format.text: 60 min: reading + listening, speaking, grammar (AI-based tasks)
Versant test on AMCAT, 60 min, automated voice-based spoken English test (Feb 2025 pool drive)
60 min; one section plays an audio only once and you repeat it (May 2025 off-campus)
60 min, 3 parts: reading, grammar and comprehension, speaking and listening

tips: Use a quiet room and a good headset mic
Speak clearly at normal speed; do not stop to correct yourself
Listen carefully, audio may play only once
stages.before_next: Practise 15 minutes of reading aloud and sentence repetition daily until it feels easy.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

stages.name: Aptitude and game-based assessment
stages.what: A quantitative aptitude section followed by short games that test speed, memory and reasoning.

format.text: Quantitative aptitude 30 questions / 30 min + 4 games / 50 min
80 min: 30 aptitude questions followed by 4 gamified sections
80 min game-based cognitive assessment on AMCAT
80 min, 40 quantitative + 40 logical reasoning questions (one older 2025 report)

tips: In the games, try to reach the highest level you can
Read each game's rules before starting
Do timed sets of 30 quant questions in 30 minutes
stages.before_next: Be able to finish 30 quant questions in 30 minutes with good accuracy.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

stages.name: Technical assessment: Coding + SQL + Web + Cloud
stages.what: An online test in your cluster language with coding problems, SQL queries, a small web (HTML/CSS/JS) task and cloud MCQs.

format.text: 120 min total: 2 coding, 2 SQL, 1 web scenario task, 10 cloud MCQs; no negative marking
120 min on AMCAT: 2 SQL, 2 programming (C#, Java or Python), 1 web development question
2 coding (Java), 2 SQL, 1 web development (HTML, CSS, JS) question; language limited to Java, Python or C#
First two sections have 4 questions in total: 2 SQL and 2 coding
GenC Next report (Nov 2025): 2 easy SQL questions on date functions, 2 Java coding questions

study: SQL: INNER/LEFT JOIN, GROUP BY, HAVING, date functions
tips: You must code in your cluster language, so practise in it, not in C++
Solve both SQL questions fully; they are usually easier
Test with edge cases before submitting
stages.before_next: Revise OOP and DBMS theory and be ready to write code live in your cluster language.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

stages.name: Technical + HR interview
stages.what: One interview that mixes technical questions, live coding and HR questions. Your category (GenC, Pro, Next) affects how hard it is.

format.text: Technical + HR interview, 30 to 45 min
GenC Next: hybrid, about 90 min, two technical panelists, 4 live coding problems on strings, arrays, OOP and SQL
Interview based on your cluster language and resume; asked about relocation and night shifts
HR part about 10 min, mostly document verification (one GenC report)

tips: Write code in the language you chose, the interviewer may refuse others
Know every line of your resume
Be ready to say yes or no to relocation and shifts honestly
stages.before_next: Keep marksheets, ID and documents ready for verification.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

stages.name: Result and category
stages.what: Cognizant reviews candidates and shares results with the placement officer (campus) or with you (off-campus). Joining happens in batches, so the joining date can come later.

format.text: Step 5: result shared with placement officer or candidate; onboarding in batches based on business demand
Shortlisted candidates are told their hiring category (GenC, GenC Pro or GenC Next)

tips: Check status on the GenC candidate platform
Ignore anyone asking for money for a job
stages.before_next: Finish your degree with no backlogs and 60%+ aggregate.
stages.label: Official

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Given two arrays, find the elements common to both.
questions.answer: Put the second array in a set, then walk the first array and keep each element found in the set (skip duplicates). Example: [1,2,2,3,4] and [2,4,6,2] gives [2,4]. O(n+m) time.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: A string contains a letter that appears twice. Find that letter.
questions.answer: Scan left to right with a set; the first character already in the set is the answer. Example: 'abca' gives 'a'. O(n) time.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Find the maximum number of consecutive 1s in a binary array.
questions.answer: Keep a running count that resets to 0 on a 0 and track the maximum. [1,1,0,1,1,1] gives 3.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Check whether a given string is a palindrome.
questions.answer: Compare the string with its reverse (s == s[::-1] in Python) or use two pointers from both ends. 'level' is a palindrome, 'hello' is not.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Count the frequency of each character in a string.
questions.answer: Use a dictionary (or collections.Counter) and add 1 for each character. 'banana' gives a:3, n:2, b:1.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Write a program to perform binary search on a sorted array of N numbers.
questions.answer: Keep low and high; check mid = (low+high)//2, move low or high depending on the comparison, stop when found or low > high. Searching 60 in [9,26,33,47,53,60,75,80,86,99] returns index 5. O(log n).
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Other
questions.question: What is the software development life cycle (SDLC)?
questions.answer: The step-by-step process for building software: requirements, design, development, testing, deployment and maintenance.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: OOP
questions.question: What are the OOP concepts? Give a real-life example.
questions.answer: Class, object, encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance and polymorphism. Example: a Car class (blueprint) and myCar (object); ElectricCar inherits Car and overrides refuel().
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: HR
questions.question: Where do you see yourself in 5 years?
questions.answer: Give a realistic growth path: strong in your tech stack, handling modules on your own, maybe guiding juniors, while growing with the company.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: HR
questions.question: Why should we hire you?
questions.answer: Link 2 or 3 real strengths to the role with proof from your projects, and show you are ready to learn the cluster tech in training.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: SQL
questions.question: Table emp(id, name, dept, salary). Write a query to list departments whose average salary is more than 50000.
questions.answer: SELECT dept, AVG(salary) FROM emp GROUP BY dept HAVING AVG(salary) > 50000; HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY, WHERE cannot use AVG.
questions.label: AI practice

questions.subject: SQL
questions.question: Tables customers(id, name) and orders(id, customer_id, amount). Show every customer with their number of orders, including customers with no orders.
questions.answer: SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name; LEFT JOIN keeps customers without orders and COUNT(o.id) gives 0 for them.
questions.label: AI practice

questions.subject: Other
questions.question: Which cloud service model gives you virtual machines, storage and networks that you manage yourself?
questions.answer: IaaS. Infrastructure as a Service gives raw compute and storage; you manage the OS and apps.
questions.label: AI practice

questions.subject: Quant
questions.question: A train 360 m long runs at 54 km/h. How long does it take to pass a pole?
questions.label: AI practice
